ab094a789e27cc17.title: Ananya Birla gets a ₹50,000 ‘Made in India’ luxury watch from Farah Khan: All about the Jaipur Watch Company piece
ab094a789e27cc17.summary: Ananya Birla, entrepreneur and singer, opened the doors of her family's Mumbai residence—the historic Jatia House bought by industrialist Kumar Mangalam Birla for ₹ 425 crore in 2018—to filmmaker Farah Khan for a new episode of her vlog ‘Food With Farah’. While the grandeur of the mansion left the director visibly impressed, a rather unique timepiece that Khan brought as a present ended up taking centre stage during the visit. Presenting the horological piece by the homegrown brand Jaipur Watch Company to Birla, Khan said, “We got you this special gift from Jaipur,” revealing that the watch was specially picked from the brand's 'Gates of India' collection. Birla, admiring the present, said, “What I love is that it is made in India.” The Main Hoon Na director also highlighted that Indian brands are now crafting one-of-a-kind luxury pieces, and pointed out, “This is a Jaipur Gate.” She also revealed that the watch has a unique reversible feature: the bezel reveals Mumbai's iconic Gateway of India on the other side. Jaipur Watch Company, a homegrown luxury watch company, said its Gates of India – Gateway of India - LOTUS embraces the heart of Jaipur's City Palace's most celebrated entrances, the Lotus Gate/the Leheriya Gate of Pritam Niwas Chowk. “More than architectural masterpieces, these gateways symbolise prosperity, renewal, and the changing seasons, welcoming generations into the royal world of art, culture, and tradition,” the company said about its yet-to-be-released product. The watchmaker, however, said that the ₹ 50,000 watch Farah Khan gifted Ananya Birla can be pre-ordered and would take upto 75 days to process. The watch, Jaipur Watch Company said, is inspired by these iconic palace gates, reimagined as a passage through India's remarkable heritage. It features a unique flip mechanism that reveals the heritage landmark of Mumbai — the Gateway of India. 063e61ccc70ec880.title: Gold imports may fall to $40 bn in FY27 on duty hike: Commerce Secy
063e61ccc70ec880.summary: India's gold imports in the current fiscal could decline to USD 40 billion, down from about USD 72 billion in FY26, as the duty hike has helped slow inbound shipments, a top official said on Wednesday. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the duty hike effected from May has "slowed down" gold imports "a bit" so far this year, from around USD 60 billion every year. This has also helped manage the trade deficit, he said. In May, the government had hiked import duty on gold and silver to 15 per cent, from 6 per cent, to contain non-essential imports. India imported USD 71.98 billion gold in FY26, up from USD 58.01 billion in FY25. Gold imports declined about 40 per cent to USD 24.78 billion during April-October this year, from about USD 41.24 billion in the corresponding period in 2025. "I think... this year we will end up with USD 35-40 billion of gold imports. I think that is manageable in the current year... The current duty structure has a positive impact on the gold import," .

17d730c28f45b3d7.title: Tata Steel plans project to produce hydrogen using steel plant off-gases
17d730c28f45b3d7.summary: Tata Steel, in partnership with Houston-based Utility Global, will undertake a project to produce hydrogen using steel plant off-gases at its Kalinganagar facility in Odisha, marking the first such initiative in the country, the company said on Wednesday. The two companies will undertake joint Front-End Engineering and Design (FEED) studies to support a Final Investment Decision (FID) by Tata Steel's board on the proposed project, it added. The proposed facility, based on Utility Global's H2Gen technology, will have a planned capacity of 10 tonnes per day (TPD) and use off-gases generated during the steelmaking process to produce high-purity hydrogen. e71a710c0506da22.title: GDP growth likely to ease to 5-quarter low of 7.5% in July-September: Icra
e71a710c0506da22.summary: India's GDP growth is estimated to slow to a five-quarter low of 7.5 per cent in July-September FY27 amid external headwinds and sub-par monsoon, rating agency ICRA said on Tuesday. The Indian economy had grown at 7.8 per cent in the first quarter (April-June) of FY27 and at 8.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2025-26 fiscal year. "The slowdown (in Q2) is expected to be mild but broad-based, led by agricultural, industrial and services sectors," ICRA said in a statement. Overall, ICRA projects the GDP growth to ease slightly to 7.5 per cent in Q2 2026-27 from 7.8 per cent in Q1 2026-27, exceeding the Monetary Policy Committee's forecast of 7.2 per cent for the quarter. ICRA estimates the farm sector to clock 0.2 per cent growth in Q2, as against 3.6 per cent in Q1 FY27. Industrial sector growth is seen at 7.2 per cent against 7.7 per cent, while the services sector is estimated at 9.1 per cent against 10 per cent. 5c353c948efc1a6c.title: Wheat sowing down 15% so far; overall rabi crops coverage falls 11%
5c353c948efc1a6c.summary: Wheat - the main rabi crop - has been sown on 50.07 lakh hectare so far this year, down by 15.27 per cent from 59.10 lakh hectare a year ago, according to data released by the Union Agriculture Ministry. The wheat crop is usually sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. In the 2025-26 crop year (July-June), wheat was planted on 336 lakh hectare. As per the latest data, the pace of wheat sowing is lagging behind as compared to last year due to the 13 per cent deficient June-September monsoon, which reduced residual soil moisture before sowing began. Experts said lower irrigation availability is another factor, with reservoir and canal water levels below normal in key wheat-growing states. Wheat requires several rounds of irrigation after planting. The Central Water Commission (CWC)'s November 12 data showed less storage in reservoirs. He said an investigation team, headed by a female officer of IPS rank, must be formed, and the matter subjected to a CB-CID inquiry. The affected Collector must not be transferred till the completion of the investigation. The Chief Minister must prove that TVK was a clean party by expelling the MLA from the party. This incident had occurred two months back and was discussed widely in the media. Besides, Villupuram Range DIG had confirmed this incident, according to a newspaper report. “That not even a single action has been taken against the MLA in a democratic country represents the height of authoritarianism. A few years ago, following a complaint by a female IPS officer who was harassed by senior police officer Rajesh Das while on security duty for the former CM, an investigation was conducted and the court awarded appropriate punishment to the perpetrator,” Mr. Tiphange said. Instead of conducting a transparent investigation in a similar manner, the TVK government was protecting the MLA. The Constitution guaranteed rights such as Article 15(3) (special protection), Article 21 (right to live with dignity), and Article 51A(e) (protecting the dignity of women). In its 'State of State Finances Report 2026-27', PRS has given an estimate of what states would have spent if the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-GRAMG), which was implemented from July 1, 2026, was in place in the 2025-26 fiscal. "The VB-GRAMG scheme is being implemented from July 1, 2026. 3d728dbcdf02d5bb.title: Ruling party MLA’s charge-sheet against govt. speaks volumes about corruption in Cong. rule: BRS
3d728dbcdf02d5bb.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:14 am IST - HYDERABAD Spokesperson of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and MLC Dasoju Sravan has stated that a ruling party MLA himself has exposed the rampant corruption and commission culture in the Congress Government. Citing recent remarks made by Jadcherla MLA Janampally Anirudh Reddy, Mr. Sravan on Tuesday demanded an answer from Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on the charges against the government by the ruling party MLA. In a statement, he said the charge-sheet against the government from within the ruling party speaks volumes of the situation. Mr. Sravan commended Mr. Anirudh Reddy for courageously speaking out against corruption within his own government. “It is not a charge-sheet from the Opposition BRS, but from a ruling party MLA himself. This is a charge-sheet released against the corrupt governance by a ruling party MLA. He has painfully exposed why contractors are fleeing the State and why development works have come to a standstill,” Mr. Sravan observed. Mr. Sravan reminded the government of the good governance promise listed as the very first item in the Congress party’s election manifesto along with the promise of corruption-free governance in the national manifesto ‘Nyay Patra’. “Earlier, when Prime Minister Narendra Modi alleged that RR Tax was being collected in Telangana, we wondered what it meant. Now, your own MLA has spoken about a 20% commission racket. This is not Praja Palana but it is Percentage Palana”, Mr. Sravan said, seeking the response of the Chief Minister. 90f6a7a237d1786a.title: My aim is to just stay focused, says shooter Vivaan Kapoor
90f6a7a237d1786a.summary: Updated - November 18, 2026 12:21 am IST Vivaan highlighted the importance of the mental side of the game. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Focus, precision and razor-sharp reflexes are the bedrock of shooting. India’s Vivaan Kapoor, however, believes the game is as much about one’s mindset. The Jaipur-born shooter calls himself a “glass-half-full guy”, and he had every reason to live up to that description after his silver-medal finish in the men’s trap event at the recent ISSF World championships. Vivaan came within touching distance of gold before losing to Kuwait’s Abdulrahman Alfaihan in a shoot-off. The silver, however, was no small feat. He secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and became only the fourth Indian man to win a trap medal at the World championships. Vivaan with his World championships silver medal. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement While the quota ensures India’s representation in the men’s trap event at Los Angeles, it does not guarantee Vivaan a place in the team. He will have to come through the National trials to earn the right to represent the country. “Standing on the podium was a dream, and there is not an iota of disappointment at missing out on gold. When you miss a target, you control your emotions and reset for the next shot. “Just like that, now, to make the Olympics cut, there’s no pressure as such. “I will not change my approach but there are some technical aspects that I need to work on. My aim is to just stay focused,” Vivaan told The Hindu. Having changed coaches just six months before the championships, Vivaan underwent an intense build-up, with three training camps under Olympic champion Giovanni Cernogoraz, two in Croatia and one in Italy. “Shooting alongside him in camps helped me get used to competing against top shooters. It made me calmer and better at controlling myself. Peter Wilson, our National coach, also helped me a lot with the mental aspect,” Vivaan said. Published - November 17, 202

e0b4baa1c5a987cc.title: Convocation ceremony row: Maharaja’s College council asks suspended students to accept their mistake
e0b4baa1c5a987cc.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:42 am IST - KOCHI A meeting of the council of Maharaja’s College, Kochi, held on Tuesday accepted an inquiry committee report that indicted activists of the Students’ Federation of India (SFI) for disrupting a convocation ceremony attended by Minister for Higher Education Roji M. John on October 30. The meeting recommended that V. Praneel Raj, chairperson, and Nafeesathul Misriya, vice-chairperson of the college union, who were suspended in connection with the incident on November 2, submit an apology admitting their mistake. The inquiry committee report found that the incident had caused disrepute to the image of the institution in the public domain, according to sources. The council observed that it did not wish to initiate further disciplinary action against the students, but they need to accept their mistake. The meeting took note of the case registered by the police against 10 SFI activists booked in connection with the protest. SFI activists staged the protest soon after the Minister completed his inaugural address at the convocation ceremony, seeking answers from him on the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady. The activists demanded that the Minister withdraw his alleged statements against those who were suspended for protesting against Vice-Chancellor Ciza Thomas. Following the protest, Mr. John had to leave the function midway. 572af06574b9e936.title: Kedarnath generates 73 tonnes of waste during 2026 Char Dham Yatra
572af06574b9e936.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 03:00 am IST - New Delhi A view of the Badrinath Temple, nestled between the Nar and Narayana mountain ranges on the bank of the Alaknanda river. File. | Photo Credit: PTI Pilgrims visiting the Kedarnath shrine generated 73 tonnes of waste during the 2026 Char Dham Yatra, more than three times the amount recorded last year. The yatra, which ended on Monday (November 16, 2026) with the closure of the Badrinath shrine portals, witnessed a record 65.65 lakh pilgrims this year. According to data shared by the civic body at Kedarnath, the 73 tonnes of waste comprised plastic bottles, food packets, Tetra Pak, and cardboard. Neeraj Kukreti, an official of the Kedarnath Nagar Panchayat, told The Hindu that waste generation this year was more than three times the 21.40 tonnes recorded in 2025. The waste generated in Kedarnath stood at 26.10 tonnes in 2024 and 32.58 tonnes in 2023, he added. To help manage the waste buildup near the temple, the district administration launched the ‘Carry Me Back’ initiative in June. The drive mobilised over 6,000 pilgrims to carry 14 tonnes of waste down to a collection point, from where it was sent for segregation and disposal.” The increase in waste generation comes amid a broader rise in pilgrim numbers across Uttarakhand’s Char Dham circuit, according to a comparative analysis released by the Dehradun-based SDC Foundation. Prepared by Anoop Nautiyal and Praveen Upreti, the study found that 65.65 lakh pilgrims visited the four Char Dham shrines — Kedarnath, Badrinath, Gangotri and Yamunotri — and Hemkund Sahib in 2026, registering a 29% increase over 51.07 lakh in 2025. The pilgrimage season extended from mid-April to mid-November. Kedarnath recorded 19,33,138 pilgrims, a 9% rise over the previous year. However, its average daily footfall declined by around 6%, from 10,113 pilgrims in 2025 to 9,476 in 2026. b506aaa32f42ba60.title: GRAP-III restrictions lifted in Delhi-NCR as air quality improves; Stage I and II curbs to remain in effect
b506aaa32f42ba60.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Tuesday revoked Stage-III restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR), citing a sustained improvement in air quality over the past three days. The decision was taken by the CAQM's GRAP Sub-Committee after reviewing the downward trend in pollution levels. However, measures under GRAP Stages I and II will continue across the NCR, along with the directions issued by the Commission in its October 30 order. Delhi's air quality remained in the 'poor' category on Tuesday morning, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 238 at 8 AM, according to the Central Pollution Control Board ( CPCB ). Of the capital's 58 monitoring stations, 31 reported 'poor' air quality, while 24 recorded 'moderate' levels. Siri Fort was the only station to report 'very poor' air quality, with an AQI of 303, according to the monitoring data. The easing of restrictions comes after Delhi's pollution levels worsened ahead of Diwali . Stage-III measures were enforced on November 6, when the city's average AQI touched 382, falling in the 'very poor' category. The restrictions were aimed at preventing further deterioration in air quality. With the withdrawal of Stage-III curbs, restrictions on certain construction and demolition activities and specified categories of vehicles will be eased. However, pollution-control measures prescribed under the first two stages of GRAP will remain operational. Favourable weather conditions and changes in the movement of pollution from neighbouring regions contributed to the recent improvement in Delhi's air quality, according to Dr Manoj Kumar, an air quality and energy analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air ( CREA ). Kumar identified northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of approximately 1,500 metres as key factors that helped disperse pollutants. The easing of restrictions comes after Delhi's pollution levels worsened ahead of Diwali . Stage-III measures were enforced on November 6, when the city's average AQI touched 382, falling in the 'very poor' category. VELANKANNI RAJ Advances in neonatal care, specialised medical infrastructure and multidisciplinary interventions are improving the survival prospects of babies born extremely prematurely, including those at the limits of viability, doctors at Rainbow Children’s Hospital said in here on Tuesday. To mark World Prematurity Day 2026, the hospital highlighted its expertise in managing periviable births, defined in India as deliveries at 24 to 25 weeks of gestation, and shared the journeys of children who overcame life-threatening complications following prolonged neonatal intensive care. Giridhar S., Clinical Lead – Neonatology, said advancements in neonatal care and the development of specialised facilities had improved survival prospects for babies born between 23 weeks and 25 weeks. He said the hospital had developed a dedicated ecosystem involving advanced ventilators, specialised incubators, round-the-clock neonatologists, a multidisciplinary team of specialists and an in-house human milk bank. Adequate nutritional support, infection control, developmental care and parental involvement were also crucial in managing extremely premature babies. “Regular eye and hearing assessments and developmental follow-up after discharge were essential,” Dr. Giridhar said. Shobana Rajendran, senior consultant neonatologist, presented the case of baby Pranav, who was born at 23 weeks weighing just 500 grams. After four-and-a-half months in the NICU, during which he required ventilator support and treatment for several complications, including extremely high blood sugar levels, he was discharged weighing two kg. 8aca1526b4d9f7d7.title: Release long-incarcerated Muslims on humanitarian grounds, says Jawahirullah
8aca1526b4d9f7d7.summary: Published - November 18, 2026 01:18 am IST - CHENNAI M.H. Jawahirullah leading the TMMK protest in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V.UMESH KUMAR Thousands of cadres of the Tamil Muslim Munnetra Kazhagam (TMMK) participated in a protest on Tuesday demanding that Muslim prisoners, who have been jailed for many years, be released on humanitarian grounds. They also sought that persons who belong to the Backward Class and Most Backward Class category, and convert to Islam, be allowed to avail 3.5% reservation meant for BC Muslims in Tamil Nadu. Speaking at he protest, Papanasam MLA M.H. Jawahirullah also criticised the TVK-led government, stating that it was not enough to just say they were supportive of Muslims. He demanded that an amendment be brought in the Assembly and passed to ensure that persons belonging to the BC and MBC be also allowed to avail the reservation. “We met the Law Minister and Public Works Minister. We met them along with former High Court Judge G.M. Akbar Ali…we spoke to them about how the Muslim prisoners can be released. They assured us that they would consider it. But, it didn’t happen. We also meet former Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, when he led the previous government. I have stressed the need to release prisoners, who had been jailed for many years, repeatedly in the Assembly. The DMK government released 41 life prisoners. Of which, 21 were Muslims,” he said. “What is stopping you from releasing the prisoners? This is why we say you are two-faced,” he said, referring to the TVK-led government. He said the TMMK had been the only movement that had been consistently speaking up for the release of such prisoners. “Many say that some of them were arrested under the Explosives Act, but the punishment is only seven years. 922a90d56dc34cd7.title: Kerala High Court allows Cusat employees to seek review of suspension
922a90d56dc34cd7.summary: Updated - November 18, 2026 01:31 am IST - KOCHI The court instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order. The Kerala High Court has held that the suspended employees of the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) can approach the university Syndicate seeking a review of their suspension. Justice P. Gopinath issued the interim direction in view of the Syndicate meeting scheduled for November 21. The court directed the Syndicate to examine whether the continued suspension was justified. It also instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order. Cusat Employees Association members Anurin Salim, P.M. Sivadas, and Harilal had approached the court challenging the suspension order. The Syndicate had suspended the petitioners based on an inquiry report by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into allegations of irregularities in appointments to the sweeper-cum-cleaner posts. They alleged that the officials were not given an opportunity to explain their position and that they were suspended before a charge memo was issued. It also instructed the petitioners to file an application before the Syndicate seeking a review of the suspension order. Cusat Employees Association members Anurin Salim, P.M. Sivadas, and Harilal had approached the court challenging the suspension order. The Syndicate had suspended the petitioners based on an inquiry report by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau (VACB) into allegations of irregularities in appointments to the sweeper-cum-cleaner posts. They alleged that the officials were not given an opportunity to explain their position and that they were suspended before a charge memo was issued. beb46b823c5f2b59.title: Delhi records Nov's cleanest air at AQI 204, but relief may be short-lived
beb46b823c5f2b59.summary: Delhi recorded its cleanest air this month on Tuesday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) settling at 204 in the 'poor' category, offering some respite after days of deteriorating air quality, though the relief is likely to be short-lived. The last time the national capital recorded a lower AQI was on October 31, when the index stood at 117 in the 'moderate' category. Tuesday's reading was the lowest recorded in November, making it the least polluted day of the month so far. The relatively better air quality on Tuesday was partly due to favourable meteorological conditions, the Air Quality Early Warning System said. Northwesterly winds reaching speeds of up to 15 kmph and a mixing depth of around 1,500 metres helped disperse pollutants. Mixing depth refers to the height up to which pollutants can disperse and mix in the atmosphere. A lower mixing depth restricts the vertical movement of pollutants, leading to their accumulation closer to the ground and potentially worsening air ...

a584679803420064.title: India's investments in US treasuries up $38.4 billion in June-August
a584679803420064.summary: India's investment in US Treasury securities increased USD 38.4 billion, or 21 per cent, between June and August, coinciding with substantial inflows of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) (B) deposits into the Indian banking system. According to data compiled by PTI from the US Department of the Treasury, India's investment in US Treasuries rose to USD 219.7 billion in August 2026 from USD 181.3 billion in May 2026, just before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the concessional facility. Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank, said the RBI's foreign exchange reserves increased during the period of FCNR(B) inflows, with a portion of the accretion being invested in US Treasury securities. The RBI had introduced a special USD-INR swap facility on June 8, 2026, to encourage foreign currency inflows and strengthen the country's balance of payments position. c3f7b46e93311ce8.title: India's edible oil import bill rises 24% to record ₹2 trillion in 2025-26
c3f7b46e93311ce8.summary: India's edible oil imports rose 6 per cent to 16.92 million tonnes in the oil year ended October 2026, and the import bill jumped 24 per cent to about Rs 200,000 crore, the Solvent Extractors' Association of India (SEA) said on Monday. Edible oil imports in the 2025-26 oil year (November-October) increased compared with 16.01 million tonnes a year earlier, when the bill was about Rs 161,126 crore, the trade body said in a statement. Total vegetable oil imports, including non-edible oils, rose 5 per cent to 17.24 million tonnes from 16.36 million tonnes. India imports edible oils to bridge the gap between domestic supply and demand, a practice that began in the 1990s. Over the past 20 years, import volumes have risen 2.8 times, while the cost has risen nearly 15 times, SEA said. Refined oil imports fell sharply to 0.82 million tonnes in 2025-26 from 1.74 million tonnes a year earlier, SEA said. 75bdaab340e1ba4a.title: Why traders are seeking GST cut from 18% to 5% - ‘Air purifiers have become as essential as medicines’
75bdaab340e1ba4a.summary: As the National Capital Region (NCR) and surrounding areas have been blanketed in toxic smog, demand for air purifiers has also risen sharply. A post-Diwali surge in demand for air purifiers, once seen as a recurring trend, is now part of a broader shift in consumer behaviour. The Tata Group entity, which operates the consumer electronics and durables retail chain Croma, said air purifier volumes have more than doubled in 2026. "North India, particularly Delhi-NCR, remains the strongest market, while Mumbai also sees an uptick during periods of poor air quality," CEO and MD Shibashish Roy was quoted as saying by news agency PTI. Amazon has also witnessed a sharp rise in demand, with air purifier sales on its platform doubling over the past week. "Air purifier sales on Amazon.in have doubled in the last week," said a company spokesperson, adding that consumers are increasingly exploring different models based on room size, filter types and features such as live AQI sensors through its AI-based shopping assistant. The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has written to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeking a reduction in the Goods and Services Tax (GST) on air purifiers, calling them "as essential as medicines", according to an Indian Express report. “With Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 400, doctors have warned that breathing the polluted air is equivalent to smoking 20-25 cigarettes a day. In such circumstances, air purifiers have become as essential as medicines. However, the 18% GST makes them expensive and puts them beyond the reach of many people,” the letter stated, according to the Indian Express report. fe34f8644c0dee12.title: Sebi may propose raising FPI beneficial ownership threshold to 25%
fe34f8644c0dee12.summary: Market regulator Sebi may propose raising the beneficial ownership identification threshold for foreign portfolio investors to 25 per cent from the current 10 per cent to ease compliance requirements and align India's regulatory framework with international best practices, an official said. The regulator is examining several areas where Indian regulations may be unnecessarily intrusive, adding to compliance costs and making the country's markets less attractive. "The regulator will soon issue another consultation paper outlining identified measures to simplify the compliance framework," he added. Citing international benchmarking, the official said several developed and emerging jurisdictions follow a 25 per cent threshold for identifying beneficial ownership. He said changes to certain provisions under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and its rules would require government intervention, while Sebi could take up other measures through its consultation process. The protest followed a letter sent by the delegation to Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on November 12, seeking an urgent meeting to discuss worsening air pollution and demand solutions. The signatories included Neha, environmentalists, Ms. Bhavreen Kandhari , Ms. Urvashi Prasad, and Capt. Ashish Jacob, among others. “We want to meet the Environment Minister and ask what the Ministry has done in the past one year to curb pollution in the city. 795ec4acd0e09879.title: IDBI Bank employee unions call one-day nationwide strike on December 3

The United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees (UFIOE), comprising the All India IDBI Officers' Association (AIIDBIOA) and the All India Industrial Development Bank Employees' Association (AIIDBEA), called the strike. Earlier this month, the UFIOE had gone on a two-day nationwide strike to oppose the proposed sale of a majority stake to Fairfax. In a strike notice served on IDBI Bank MD and CEO, the UFIOE said the strike would be observed across all branches and offices of the bank nationwide. The unions have demanded that the government and LIC stop the proposed sale of IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings, describing the bank as a national asset. The unions have also warned they will intensify their agitation if their demands are not met, including strikes lasting more than one day and even an indefinite

c347fb3e4c447c3d.title: FinMin examining suggestions for changes in equity capital gains tax: CBDT
c347fb3e4c447c3d.summary: The Finance Ministry is examining various aspects of capital gains tax on equities, and probable changes in taxation would come in the Union Budget for 2027-28, a senior official said on Monday. Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Chairman Ravi Agrawal said the ministry is considering suggestions from various stakeholders made during the pre-budget meetings. "We will consider it, and I'm sure on February 1 you will get to know. Analysis is being done of whatever issues have been flagged or points that have been raised by the stakeholders," Agrawal told reporters on the sidelines of the inauguration of a CBDT lounge at the IITF here. Agrawal said the different facets of the capital gains tax regime, including tax implications, will be examined, and the decision will be announced in the Budget. Industry chambers have already made representations to the Ministry recommending abolition of Long Term Capital Gains tax (LTCG). They also suggested rationalising short-term capital gains .

59377c3dc3ee9694.title: Chennai Corporation opens free public toilets at 853 locations
59377c3dc3ee9694.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:25 am IST - Chennai The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) has completed and opened free public toilets at 853 locations across Chennai, providing 7,644 seats, against its target of 10,444 at 1,479 locations. Work is under way at 193 locations, accounting for 1,270 seats, while steps have been initiated to establish facilities at another 433 locations with 1,530 seats, according to a press release issued on November 15. The figures leave 626 locations, with a total of 2,800 seats, yet to be completed under the scheme. Of these, facilities at 193 locations are under construction. The latest figures were released after GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran inspected a free public toilet at Anna Nagar Tower Park on Sunday. He interacted with members of the public to enquire about the use and maintenance of the facility. The GCC said the toilets were being designed to provide safe access for senior citizens, persons with disabilities, children, and transgender persons. Each facility has a worker appointed for cleaning and maintenance. Workers are provided with gloves, masks, and footwear, besides training in safety protocols, handling chemicals, and personal hygiene. A QR code facility has also been provided at the toilets for users to submit feedback and complaints. The complaints are monitored and addressed within a specified timeframe, with updates on their status sent to users, the release said. In February, the GCC held community consultation meetings at 437 locations where free public toilets had been established. The meetings, held across all 15 zones under the campaign ‘Our toilet, our responsibility’, covered issues such as cleanliness, maintenance, accessibility, water quality, and public safety. The February release did not specify the total number of toilet seats in operation. The GCC said it would consider establishing more toilets at its parks and burial grounds based on public demand. Published - November 17, 2026 12:25 am IST Ter

3cc95212521891fe.title: India’s unemployment rate dips to 4.9% in October on urban recovery
3cc95212521891fe.summary: New Delhi: India’s unemployment rate for those aged 15 years and above fell marginally to 4.9% in October from 5% in September as joblessness fell in urban areas but remained steady in rural centres, according to the latest Periodic Labour Force Survey Monthly Bulletin (PLFS-M) released by the statistics ministry on Monday. The unemployment rate in urban areas fell to 6.7% in October from 6.9% the previous month, driven primarily by a sharp fall in unemployment rate among urban women – from 9.2% in September to 8.7% in October. The unemployment rate , however, remained steady at 6% among urban men. The unemployment rate in rural areas remained static at 4.2% in October but remained well below the 4.4% level registered in October 2025. In rural areas, the unemployment rate fell both among men and women. While the unemployment rate fell back to 4.3% in October from 4.4% in the previous month among rural men, it fell to 3.8% from 3.9% among rural women. Compared with October, 2025, the overall unemployment actually fell from 5.2% to 4.9%. The rural unemployment rate declined by 0.2 percentage points from 4.4% in October 2025 to 4.2% in October 2026. It fell more sharply in urban areas, from 7% in October 2025 to 6.7% in October 2026, the ministry of statistics and programme implementation ( MoSPI ) said. According to the ministry, the overall unemployment rate among men aged 15 years and above remained stable at 4.9% in October 2026 compared with the previous month, continuing the downward or stable trend observed since June 2026. The unemployment rate among women declined across both rural and urban areas, falling overall to 5% in October from 5.2% in September, the ministry said. For rural women, the rate dropped to 3.8%—its lowest level in 2026. The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is the primary official source of data on employment and unemployment in India. Since January 2025, its methodology has been updated to provide monthly and quarterly national estimates

Nethram - Universal Newborn Eye Screening (UNES), a specially curated newborn eye-screening package was also launched to safeguard infants’ visual health from the very beginning. 082889053e29620a.title: Committee to inspect Valagerahalli Lake
082889053e29620a.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 01:00 am IST - Bengaluru The Lokayukta has acted on a petition filed by local residents, who raised concerns over the deteriorating condition of Valagerahalli Lake and the health hazards it poses. After examining the complaints and a report submitted by the executive engineer of the lake division of the Bengaluru West City Corporation, the Lokayukta observed that sewage was entering the lake along with rainwater. The Lokayukta expressed concern over the lack of adequate action by the authorities to prevent pollution and protect the lake. A joint inspection committee comprising the Chief Engineer (TAC) of the Karnataka Lokayukta, Superintendent of Police-1, Karnataka Lokayukta, and officials of the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board has been constituted. The committee has been directed to inspect the lake, assess its present condition, and submit a report with recommendations by November 30. The Lokayukta said action would be initiated against officials found guilty of dereliction of duty if steps were not taken to resolve the issue. ec92f89f9a9b7221.title: Events lined up for National Newborn Week at Government Stanley Hospital
ec92f89f9a9b7221.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:01 am IST - CHENNAI The Institute of Social Paediatrics, Government Stanley Medical College Hospital, is observing the “National Newborn Week” from November 15 to November 21 to create awareness about scientific newborn care, and to dispel prevailing myths and misconceptions. According to a press release, the theme for 2026 is “Small Babies, Big Potential. Invest in Follow-up Care to Protect Their Future”, highlighting the importance of regular follow-up and developmental monitoring of small babies. As part of the celebrations, hospital dean S. Jothikumar and institute’s director J. Ganesh distributed newborn care awareness pamphlets to nursing mothers and the public on Monday, and interacted with them to clarify their doubts. The week-long celebrations include educational sessions for nursing mothers on newborn care, Neonatal Resuscitation Programme training for undergraduate and postgraduate medical students, a session on prevention of sepsis for Newborn Intensive Care Unit staff nurses, a mentor visit to Thiruvottiyur Urban Primary Health Centre, and a lecture on Essential Newborn Care for nursing students. According to Sample Registration System 2024 data, India’s Neonatal Mortality Rate and Infant Mortality Rate are 18 and 24 per 1,000 live births, respectively, while Tamil Nadu has achieved lower rates of eight and 11 respectively. However, continued efforts are essential to further reduce preventable newborn deaths, the release said. Vice-principal R. Sathya Lakshmi and Resident Medical Officer Vanithamalar participated. d4ee39faf0d39627.title: 70% turnout in most districts as four-phase panchayat polls end in Rajasthan
d4ee39faf0d39627.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 01:34 am IST - JAIPUR The four-phase panchayat election process in Rajasthan concluded on Monday with polling held for 3,747 sarpanch and 33,885 ward panch posts across 25 districts. Voting exceeded 70% in most of the districts that went to the polls in the final phase. There were stray incidents of confrontation and violence at some places, though long queues of voters were seen at several polling stations since morning. Villagers in Jalore district’s Gundau and Bharatpur district’s Shakarpur staged protests and created a ruckus raising allegations of bogus voting. Police fired in the air and used force to disperse the supporters of two rival candidates for the sarpanch post at Mahu Gulawali in Dholpur district. The two groups clashed and hurled stones at each other, while one of them set on fire two motorcycles parked outside a polling booth. In Dholpur’s Baroli village, polling started in late afternoon amid tension over a shooting incident on Sunday that resulted in the death of one person following a clash over election-related rivalry. Police have detained the main accused and 10 others in connection with the incident. The allegations of fraudulent voting sparked tension in Kali Pahadi village of Khairthal-Tijara district and a verbal altercation between two groups escalated into a physical confrontation. Police arrived in the village on receiving information and brought the situation under control. An elderly person, who sustained serious injuries during the clash, was referred to Alwar for treatment. Voting for both sarpanch and ward panch posts was conducted through ballot papers. More than 1.05 crore voters were eligible to exercise their franchise at 11,905 polling stations. Counting of votes started immediately after the polling ended. 26e7ae12664ae0fd.title: India's sugar output more than doubles to 2.35 mn tonnes by Nov 15: ISMA
26e7ae12664ae0fd.summary: India's sugar production more than doubled to 23.59 lakh tonne in the ongoing 2026-27 season through November 15, as mills in top producer Maharashtra started crushing early, the Indian Sugar & Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association (ISMA) said on Monday. Output stood at 11.49 lakh tonne in the same period a year earlier, the industry body said. The sugar season runs from October to September, with crushing typically starting in October-November. The sweetener's production in Maharashtra, the country's biggest producer, jumped more than threefold to 18.51 lakh tonne from 5.25 lakh tonne a year earlier. Mills in the western state began crushing from October 8, earlier than in other states, and 154 mills were operating as of November 15, against 132 a year ago. Output in Uttar Pradesh, the second-biggest producer, fell to 2.10 lakh tonne from 4.25 lakh tonne, with 80 mills operational compared with 88 a year earlier. In Karnataka, the third-largest producer, output was little changed .

4bf63a7730979edd.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:58 am IST - Bengaluru The RTI application, filed by a Jayanagar resident, had specifically sought details of the project, the feasibility assessment and approvals or NOCs issued by the BWSSB to ensure that its pipelines would not be disturbed by the proposed construction. The Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) has clarified that it has not granted any approval or issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the proposed 18.5-km Ragigudda-Kanakapura Road elevated corridor, which is planned along a water pipeline alignment in south Bengaluru. The Board also stated that it does not have the project’s feasibility report or related technical documents on record. The clarification, issued on October 29 in response to a Right to Information (RTI) application filed on September 18, has only added to the concerns raised by residents opposing the project, who have warned that construction along the alignment could put major Cauvery water pipelines supplying south Bengaluru at risk. In its reply, the Executive Engineer’s Office said the feasibility report and related technical documents of the proposed elevated corridor were not available in its office. It also categorically stated that the Board had not issued any approval or NOC for construction of any structure along the said route. The RTI application, filed by a Jayanagar resident, had specifically sought details of the project, the feasibility assessment and approvals or NOCs issued by the BWSSB to ensure that its pipelines would not be disturbed by the proposed construction. According to a representation submitted by residents under the banner ‘Citizens from South Bengaluru’, four major water mains run along the proposed alignment — three measuring 1,200 mm in diameter and one measuring 1,750 mm. 1ce65c42fd8a5905.title: IISc researchers combine antibiotics to tackle drug-resistant TB
1ce65c42fd8a5905.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:49 am IST - Bengaluru Bacteria which cause tuberculosis Mycobacterium tuberculosis, 3D illustration Researchers at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), have identified a strategy to restore the effectiveness of isoniazid, a frontline drug used to treat tuberculosis (TB), caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis). According to the IISc, TB caused by M. tuberculosis, continues to remain one of the world’s most persistent health challenges. However, it said that what’s particularly alarming is the bacterium’s growing resistance to isoniazid. Now, researchers at the Department of Biochemistry have now identified a strategy to restore the effectiveness of isoniazid – by combining it with another antibiotic, vancomycin. They found that this combination can reverse isoniazid resistance in clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis and reduce bacterial burden in a mouse model. “Isoniazid resistance poses a major challenge in the treatment of TB. To tackle this problem, we started exploring ways to rescue the drug by reversing resistance,” said Nagasuma Chandra, Professor at the Department of Biochemistry and corresponding author of the study published in Microbiology Spectrum . PhD student and first author of the study, Sukriti Pal said that although several antibiotic combinations are available for TB treatment challenges presist due to drug-resistance. She said that the new study identifies a drug treatment strategy that can reverse resistance to isoniazid, an otherwise highly effective antibiotic. The researchers tested the combination of isoniazid and vancomycin against clinical isolates of M. tuberculosis obtained from patient sputum samples with drug-resistant TB, in collaboration with the National Tuberculosis Institute, Bengaluru. 6ade28a1b9578697.title: Chennai hospital treats 5-year-old girl with rare ‘Dancing Eye Syndrome’
6ade28a1b9578697.summary: Published - November 17, 2026 12:19 am IST - Chennai Dr. Mehta’s Hospitals treated a five-year-old girl with Opsoclonus Myoclonus Ataxia Syndrome (OMAS), a.k.a. Dancing Eye Syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder associated with a thoracic tumour located adjacent to the aorta, the main artery that carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body. The team, led by M. Raghul, pediatric surgeon, performed minimally invasive surgery to remove the tumour. Shivan Kesavan, pediatric neurologist, treated the child for OMAS. The girl was brought to the hospital for treatment in April this year following darting eye movements, slurred speech, leg pain and involuntary jerking of the head. “Removing a thoracic tumour that is densely adherent to the aorta and the chest wall has its own complexities. Performing this through a minimally invasive thoracoscopic approach is technically challenging. Despite these complexities, the team removed the tumour completely, avoiding the need for an open thoracotomy,” said Dr. Raghul. She was discharged in May 2026 and during a recent follow-up visit with Dr. Raghul, the child had made a remarkable recovery, was fully active, and showed no signs of her earlier symptoms. Dr. Shivan Kesavan, Pediatric Neurologist, Dr. Mehta’s Hospitals spoke about the need for awareness of OMAS. 329ab65fdbfcace7.title: TVS' Lakshmi Venu seeks partition of family assets, escalating family feud
329ab65fdbfcace7.summary: Lakshmi Venu, a member of the TVS industrial family, has formally sought a partition of the joint family assets of her father Venu Srinivasan's branch, escalating a succession dispute that could have implications for ownership and control of key businesses within one of India's best-known automobile groups. In a partition notice to her father, Lakshmi called on him, as head of the family, to discharge his fiduciary duties and ensure a "fair and lawful partition," according to a statement from her office on Monday. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has publicly backed her claim, exposing a deepening rift within the family over the distribution of its wealth. Lakshmi maintains that she is entitled to an equal share under the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, and has an independent right to seek partition. She has invoked Section 6 of the Act, which recognises daughters as coparceners with the same rights as sons in qualifying Hindu joint family property. The claim covers

68b71d3440fb4120.title: M.P. CM announces crop loss survey, financial aid for farmers in rain deficit Alirajpur district
68b71d3440fb4120.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 01:21 am IST - Bhopal Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Sunday announced a crop loss survey in Alirajpur to provide financial assistance to the farmers in the State’s worst rain-deficit district. Addressing a Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas programme, marking the birth anniversary of tribal icon Birsa Munda, in Jhobat, the CM announced he was issuing instructions to the District Collector to begin the survey and provide aid to farmers affected by rain deficiency. “I am issuing directions to the Collector to conduct a survey and help them as per the Revenue Book Circular (RBC) 6-4. You will get money in your accounts from the government,” he said. At least 11 districts of Madhya Pradesh have experienced severe rainfall deficit, with those in the Nimar and Malwa regions being the worst hit. It severely impacted kharif crops like soybean. Alirajpur, that falls under the Nimar region, recorded nearly 52% lower rainfall than normal. The government, though, has not announced such surveys in other affected districts, even as officials claim that discussions on relief measures are going on. Earlier in the day, Chief Minister and Governor Mangubhai Patel inaugurated ₹1,353.18 crore Dahi Micro Lift Irrigation Project in Dhar’s Dahi, which aims to provide irrigation through Narmada water to 47,000 hectares of agricultural land across 84 villages in Dhar and and 42 in Alirajpur districts. According to government officials, about a lakh farmers are likely to benefit directly from the project’s permanent irrigation facility. Last month, Mr. Yadav had launched another micro-lift irrigation project worth around ₹2,400-crore in Dhar’s Sardarpur. 3f12a661b2bffce7.title: Govt health spending triples, household burden eases
3f12a661b2bffce7.summary: New Delhi: India's government health spending nearly tripled over a decade, while households' share of the country's total healthcare bill fell sharply, pointing to a gradual shift away from out-of-pocket financing towards public funding. The share of healthcare expenditure borne by households declined to 42.7% in 2023-24 from 64.2% in 2013–14, according to the National Health Accounts (NHA) estimates released by the Union health ministry on Sunday. “The simultaneous increase in public healthcare financing and decline in the proportion of spending borne directly by households reflects India's progress towards a more accessible, affordable and financially protective healthcare system,” the ministry said in a release. Government health expenditure rose to ₹ 4.14 trillion in 2023-24 from ₹ 1.30 trillion in 2013-14. Its share of total health expenditure increased by 14.9 percentage points over the period, while per capita public health spending rose 2.8 times, from ₹ 1,042 to ₹ 2,959. “The most important development is the changing balance between public and household contributions to healthcare expenditure. A larger share of total healthcare spending is now being financed through government resources, while a considerably smaller share is being borne directly by households,” the ministry said. Primary healthcare received ₹ 1.53 trillion in government funding, supporting the rollout of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. These centres offer preventive care, screening for non-communicable diseases , medicines and diagnostic tests at the community level. Financial protection through health coverage schemes also expanded. Social security expenditure on health, which includes government-funded insurance programmes such as Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), state health insurance schemes, social health insurance and medical reimbursements for government employees, rose from 6% of total health expenditure in 2013–14 to 11% in 2023–24. 3981500cbc480836.title: Goyal meets ElSewedy Electric CEO, discusses India investment opportunities
3981500cbc480836.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal met Ahmed ElSewedy, President and CEO of the Egyptian multinational ElSewedy Electric, to discuss potential investment opportunities in India. "We discussed strategies to strengthen collaboration across several key sectors, including electrical equipment, smart meters, and data centres," Goyal said in a social media post. As India enters a significant growth trajectory, the country's expansive market presents substantial opportunities for global enterprises to invest, innovate, and expand, he added. Goyal is here on a two-day visit. He is leading a 132-member business delegation. During his visit, he will meet business and Egyptian leaders to discuss ways to boost bilateral trade and investments.

1f988140e5391ad1.title: Chhath Puja: Despite politics over Yamuna, Delhi stretch of river continues to be polluted
1f988140e5391ad1.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 02:22 am IST - New Delhi Devotees gather along the banks of the Yamuna, polluted with toxic foam, during the Chhath Puja festival in Noida on Sunday. | Photo Credit: PTI Despite the political slugfest over the Yamuna during yet another Chhath Puja, official data show that the river’s Delhi stretch remains heavily polluted for most of the year, with water quality improving during the monsoon, when floodwaters flush out pollutants. According to official data, the faecal coliform level (microbes from human and animal excreta) in the Yamuna at Asgarpur, where the river leaves the Capital, was 660 times the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) desirable limit for bathing water quality in May, before the monsoon. The water quality improved in September, as it does every year after the monsoon. The Delhi government has yet to make the October data public. The Yamuna holds religious significance for people from Purvanchal (residents of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar), who constitute a significant voter base in Delhi. Many observe Chhath Puja by taking a dip in the river. Scores of devotees offered prayers at Kalindi Kunj in south Delhi on Sunday evening, standing knee-deep in the river as toxic froth floated on the water — a familiar sight during Chhath Puja. Since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in February 2025, an ambitious plan to divert water from the Ganga to flush out pollutants from the Delhi stretch of the Yamuna has been under discussion. However, it has yet to yield any concrete results. The proposal formed part of a broader plan to clean the river, which was presented to Prime Minister Narendra Modi in April last year. Following his approval, Union Home Minister Amit Shah has held several review meetings on the plan, according to sources. “Even if the plan is finalised, it will take about two to three years for Ganga water to reach Delhi. 3110698f7355fd13.title: Thomas Cook India expects demerger of resorts business by Oct 2027: MD
3110698f7355fd13.summary: Thomas Cook (India) Ltd expects the proposed demerger of its resorts and resort-management business into Sterling Holiday Resorts to become effective by October 2027, according to a top company official. In an interview with PTI, Mahesh Iyer, Managing Director and CEO of Thomas Cook (India) Ltd, said the company expects the scheme to become effective by mid-FY28. "The application in respect of the composite scheme of arrangement has been filed before NCLT Mumbai. Accordingly, we expect the scheme to become effective by mid of FY28. However, the same is subject to the requisite regulatory and shareholder approvals," Iyer shared. In March, the Board of Thomas Cook (India) Ltd (TCIL) approved a proposal for the demerger of the company's Resorts and Resort Management business into Sterling Holiday Resorts Ltd (SHRL) and a subsequent capital restructuring of TCIL. Separately, on the company's inorganic growth strategy, Iyer said, Thomas Cook India remained open to exploring acquisitions

62638b013bdba781.title: NCW calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi issue
62638b013bdba781.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 12:42 am IST - CHENNAI The National Commission for Women (NCW) has written to the Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police seeking a fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations that “C. Arul Vignesh, MLA from Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu, sent obscene WhatsApp messages to J.E. Padmaja, District Collector, Kallakurichi.” The NCW in a social media post said its chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has written to the DGP, Tamil Nadu, seeking a “fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations, including examination of the representations reportedly made by the District Collector to senior officials and the action taken thereon.” The Commission, which took suo motu cognisance of a media report, has called for the preservation and examination of relevant digital evidence and emphasised that the matter must be investigated without any political or external influence, irrespective of the position held by the person concerned, according to its social media post. “The Commission has sought a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days. The dignity, safety and security of women public officials must be upheld without exception. No position or influence can place anyone above accountability for alleged harassment or misconduct,” it said. Published - November 16, 2026 12:42 am IST

6f3a68895a1f4b6e.summary: Foreign investors made a strong comeback to Indian equities in the first fortnight of November, pumping in Rs 84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows, amid a global AI sell-off, falling crude prices and attractive large-cap valuations. The latest inflows follow net withdrawals of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data from the depositories. According to the data, Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) made a net investment of Rs 84,290 crore in Indian equities during November 2-13, covering nine trading sessions. With the latest inflows, cumulative FPI outflows from Indian equities have narrowed to around Rs 2.1 lakh crore in 2026 from nearly Rs 3 lakh crore a few weeks ago. d96f950228b38b31.title: Hyderabad hospital performs combined heart valve procedures in single sitting
d96f950228b38b31.summary: Published - November 16, 2026 12:29 am IST - HYDERABAD Doctors at Apollo Hospitals in Hyderabad performed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) and Balloon Mitral Valvotomy (BMV) on an 83-year-old man in a single sitting on Saturday. The procedure was performed by cardiologists P.C. Rath and Manoj Kumar Agarwala during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting. The patient, who had previously undergone coronary artery bypass surgery and pacemaker implantation, was admitted with severe aortic and mitral valve stenosis. Doctors opted for a minimally invasive intervention involving the replacement of the aortic valve and balloon dilatation of the mitral valve. Both procedures were successfully performed through the femoral artery, accessed through the groin, under anaesthesia. The intervention was also demonstrated live during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting. Hyderabad is hosting leading interventional cardiologists and structural heart specialists from all over the world for Hyderabad Valves 2026, the fourth edition of a biennial scientific meeting focused on modern, minimally invasive treatments for heart valve disease. The meeting brought together Indian and international experts for live case demonstrations, specialist lectures and interactive discussions on complex valve and structural heart interventions. The conference features 26 live transcatheter cases from centres in India and overseas. The programme includes 11 live-case transmissions from leading international centres, including four from the USA, and six each from Europe and Apollo Hospitals, Jubilee Hills. Each demonstration provides an opportunity for specialists to discuss clinical decisions, procedural techniques and patient safety. 527deebf21524cf2.summary: India has voted against a draft UN General Assembly resolution calling on nations to establish a moratorium on the death penalty. The 193-member UNGA adopted by recorded vote the resolution on Friday introduced by Mexico on 'Moratorium on the use of the death penalty', with 133 countries voting in favour of the resolution, 33 against and 16 abstentions. India, along with Bahrain, China, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Japan, Kuwait, Maldives, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the US, voted against the resolution. The resolution expressed deep concern about the continued application of the death penalty and reaffirmed the right of all countries to develop their own legal systems, including determining appropriate legal penalties in accordance with international law. It called upon all States to establish a moratorium on executions, with a view to abolishing the death penalty. 5d58a040bd292fc2.title: Couple from Tumakuru end their lives in Udupi district
5d58a040bd292fc2.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 10:44 pm IST - MANGALURU A 52-year-old man and his 48-year-old wife ended their lives by jumping off a bridge across the Seeta River, in Mabukala, Udupi district, on Saturday night, the Udupi district police said. The police said the deceased have been identified as as H. Srinivas Murthy and Ganga. According to the police, the couple were on a visit to pilgrimage places in the Karavali and Malnad regions. After visiting Murudeshwar in Uttara Kannada district, the couple came to Mabukala on Saturday evening. An autorickshaw driver saw the couple jump off the bridge after walking a few metres. He immediately called the police and reported the incident. The police carried out a search operation in association with firemen and local swimmers on Sunday morning. The bodies of the couple were found about 500 metres down the bridge. The reason for their decision to end their lives was unknown. A case has been registered at the Kota Police Station, and the bodies have been kept in a mortuary at the Government Hospital in Kundapur. The police were waiting for the family members of the deceased couple to arrive to continue their investigation. 073cb5355e462578.title: Sabarimala sets target of 75 pilgrims a minute on holy steps
073cb5355e462578.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 07:30 pm IST As many as 75 pilgrims are expected to climb the 18 holy steps to the Sabarimala shrine every minute under a new crowd management target set by the authorities for the annual pilgrimage season, which kicks off on Tuesday. Devaswom Minister K. Muraleedharan said the police had been given necessary directions to achieve the target. Senior police officers were also reviewing the arrangements on the instructions of the Home Minister. The Minister also sought to dismiss concerns over the availability of appam and aravana during the season. He said his visit to the production centre had convinced him of the efforts being made by employees to ensure uninterrupted production by working round the clock.”The Devaswom Board had assured us that the pilgrimage season could be completed smoothly if 75 lakh tins of aravana were made available,” he said. He also assured that the State government would release the first instalment of payments due to local self-government bodies for setting up facilities for pilgrims within a couple of days. Instructions had also been issued to ensure adequate stocks of medicines at healthcare centres. All government departments involved in the pilgrimage arrangements were working in coordination to discharge their responsibilities, he said. Preparations for next year’s pilgrimage season would begin as soon as the current season concluded. The government had decided to launch infrastructure development works for the next season as early as February, after the temple closes following the pilgrimage season, the Minister added. 519bf9abeba60aa0.title: SpaceX makes first launch pad catch of Starship after its orbital return
519bf9abeba60aa0.summary: SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for - the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday's liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad. The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster's messy miss. "Can you believe it?" shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot. SpaceX officials said Saturday's catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. 97a374f93eb9025b.title: Measure AI by results, not number of agents deployed: Oracle's executive
97a374f93eb9025b.summary: Businesses adopting artificial intelligence (AI) should start with a measurable goal and judge success by the improvement it delivers rather than the number of AI agents deployed, as the technology moves from helping employees to doing work for them, a senior Oracle executive said. "It's important to remember that the number of agents deployed matters less than the improvement they deliver," Natalia Rachelson, Senior Vice President, Applications Development at Oracle, told PTI. Business leaders should pick an outcome they can measure, such as reducing the time spent resolving accounting errors or lowering transport costs, she said. "It's important to establish a baseline first so you can assess whether AI is making a meaningful difference," she noted. Companies then need to get the basics right: reliable data, clear ownership of processes, appropriate controls, and employees who understand how to work with AI agents. 27a1d194fb48bef3.title: 200 patients receive medical services at health camp
27a1d194fb48bef3.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 11:41 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Around 200 patients received medical services at a camp organised by Praja Arogya Vedika (PAV) and Jana Vignana Vedika in Vijayawada on Sunday. The camp provided medical services, including consultations, medicines, guidance to patients suffering from diabetes, hypertension, epilepsy and paralysis at a minimal consultation fee. Later, volunteers distributed the required tablets and insulin to the patients and explained how to take the medicine. PAV NTR district general secretary G. Vijay Prakash said such camps were being held once every two months for the benefit of the public, and the next one will be held on January 17. A medical team from HCG Cancer Hospital also conducted free cancer screening tests for patients at the camp. 311ec4d9593f0875.title: CIAL sets up facilitation centre for Sabarimala pilgrims
311ec4d9593f0875.summary: Updated - November 15, 2026 06:50 pm IST - KOCHI Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) has set up a dedicated pilgrim facilitation centre at the airport for Sabarimala pilgrims. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the centre on November 17. Spread across 5,000 sq. ft., the centre is located near the police aid post, adjacent to the domestic arrival terminal and will remain open round the clock. KSRTC bus services are available to and from the airport from here, with a booking counter set up at the centre. Pilgrims can also book chartered bus services on demand. A dedicated counter for helicopter service bookings has also been arranged. The other facilities at the centre include a Devaswom help desk, prasadam coupon counter, prepaid taxi booking facility, vegetarian food outlet, and a rest area. A flight information display system has also been installed to provide real-time flight updates. Its proximity to the domestic terminal makes the centre easily accessible to pilgrims, says an official release. Around 11,000 pilgrims made use of the facilitation centre last year, including those from Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Malaysia, and Singapore, it says. 650fba9c6486b78e.title: Govt mandates scrutiny of 'abnormally low bids', sets 30% threshold
650fba9c6486b78e.summary: The finance ministry has made it mandatory for government agencies to scrutinise bids quoting prices more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost in a government procurements, tightening checks on abnormally low bids to safeguard service and product quality. The Department of Expenditure under the ministry has defined Abnormally Low Bids (ALBs) in government procurement, mandating scrutiny of bids falling below the prescribed threshold and seeking written clarifications wherever "concerns" arise over the bidder's ability to execute the contract at the quoted price. "A bid quoting a price more than 30 per cent below the estimated cost shall mandatorily be examined as a potentially ALB," the department said in an office memorandum. In such cases, the procuring entity would seek written clarifications from the bidder, including detailed price analyses of its bid price in relation to scope of work as given in the tender document. d321864c04d665c0.title: Drug de-addiction awareness programme at VSP
d321864c04d665c0.summary: Published - November 15, 2026 11:26 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM To mark the sixth anniversary of the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), Visakha Steel General Hospital (VSGH) of Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL), in association with Ukkunagaram Brahma Kumaris, organised a drug de-addiction awareness programme at the Learning and Development Centre auditorium in Ukkunagaram, according to a release in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. Speaking as chief guest, RINL Director (Commercial) G.V.N. Prasad underscored the organisation’s commitment to employee well-being. Describing substance abuse as a critical public health challenge, he stressed the need for timely medical intervention, counselling, and rehabilitation alongside collective community support. Guest speaker B.K.K. Yashwanth, Associate Professor of General Surgery at NRIIMS, detailed the physiological and psychological impacts of prolonged substance dependence on vital organs, highlighting lifestyle modifications and sustained support for recovery. The event featured a guided Raja Yoga meditation session by Ukkunagaram Brahma Kumaris focusing on mindfulness and mental resilience, an interactive Q&A on relapse prevention, and the administration of the NMBA pledge. 8f9e5dc91f822f2a.summary: A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday. Rains are expected to occur in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said. According to the latest weather report, Saturday's well marked low pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5.30 am today. It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of south and adjoining west central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17. The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the state from Monday. 6879830d61ccf3b9.title: USFDA closes Dr Reddy's Hyderabad facility inspection with VAI status
6879830d61ccf3b9.summary: Dr Reddy's Laboratories has said the US health regulator classified the inspection outcome of its formulations manufacturing facility here as 'Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI)' and officially closed the inspection. In a regulatory filing on Saturday, the company said the Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) inspection was conducted by the USFDA at its formulations manufacturing facility (FTO-3) in Bachupally, Hyderabad. The company had earlier informed the stock exchanges regarding the inspection on August 14, 2026. "We wish to inform you that the United States Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) has classified the inspection outcome as 'Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI)' and concluded that the inspection is officially closed under 21 CFR 20.64(d)(3)," Dr Reddy's said in the filing.

Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. 188773d87bdae077.summary: Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering. More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016. Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year. By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. 9fd615d49438ee16.summary: Updated - November 16, 2026 01:21 am IST - GURUGRAM Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders. Organised on the call of the Rajkiya Anubandhit Adhyapak Sangh, the symbolic Assembly passed a resolution seeking regularisation of guest teachers by an overwhelming majority. The resolution will be submitted to Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini at his camp office in Kurukshetra on November 29. The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President. Teachers said guest teachers had been serving in government schools for the past 21 years and contributing to the State’s education system, but the government continued to keep them in temporary employment arrangements instead of regularising their services. Following the court orders, the Haryana School Education Department issued speaking orders denying regular status to the guest teachers. They said the mock Assembly was organised to raise questions concerning the regularisation of guest teachers, judicial decisions and the government’s accountability on a public platform. The event was attended by educationists, intellectuals, employee union leaders from various departments, School Management Committee representatives, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, student and youth organisations, advocates’ unions, writers’ associations, university professors, the Jan Sangharsh Manch, Kurukshetra, and social activists. These teachers, appointed between 2005 and 2008, are working as junior basic teachers, trained graduate teachers, and post graduate teachers. He further urged Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. He alleged that corruption was rampant during both the previous AIADMK government led by Edappadi K Palaniswami and DMK government led by M.K. Stalin. Claiming that commissions had been fixed at specific percentages in various departments, he said that even teachers and nurses had to pay bribes amounting to several thousand rupees to secure transfers. However, the present government led by Mr. Vijay follows a policy of integrity, he noted. Stalin should take responsibility for the alleged irregularities, describing the incident as a major attack on the world of knowledge and learning. He demanded that a committee be constituted to investigate the matter and stringent punishment be imposed on everyone found responsible. He further expressed confidence that the alliance led by Chief Minister Joseph Vijay would register a landslide victory in the upcoming by-elections as well as the next assembly elections. 8b7759995151af33.title: ONGC takes over disputed Cambay block from Vedanta after court ruling
8b7759995151af33.summary: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies. Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block. The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing. The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent. The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC. Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court

2ff26f97a71862cf.title: Sammaan Capital Q2 FY27 results: Net profit rises 1.25% to ₹312 crore
2ff26f97a71862cf.summary: Non-bank lender Sammaan Capital on Saturday reported a 1.25 per cent increase in its September quarter net profit to Rs 312.34 crore compared to Rs 308.47 crore in the same quarter of last year. The company had reported a net profit of Rs 243.30 crore in the preceding June quarter. Its total income declined to Rs 1,850.85 crore in the reporting quarter from Rs 2,260.52 crore in the year-ago period, which included a decline in the core interest income to Rs 1,161.26 crore from Rs 1,449.02 crore. Total expenses also declined to Rs 1,426.28 crore from Rs 1,835.49 crore in the year-ago period, as per a regulatory filing. Assets under management grew by 5 per cent to Rs 59,188 crore as of end-June 2026, driven by a 62 per cent jump in disbursements to Rs 6,278 crore. It aims to increase AUM to Rs 70,000 crore by March 2027. The company added more branches during the quarter to take its overall network to 245 as of September 30, and is aiming to take the same to 270 by end of the fiscal
